statement: For $a>1$, let $f(x)=a^{x}+a^{-x}$. Show that $f(x)$ has a minimum at $x=0$ and find the minimum value. Hence solve $2^{x}+2^{-x}=5$.
solution: By AM-GM, $a^{x}+a^{-x}\\ge2\\sqrt{a^{x}a^{-x}}=2$, with equality when $a^{x}=a^{-x}$, i.e. $x=0$. So the minimum value is $2$ at $x=0$. For $2^{x}+2^{-x}=5$, set $u=2^{x}>0$ to get $u+u^{-1}=5$, so $u^{2}-5u+1=0$ and $u=\\frac{5\\pm\\sqrt{21}}{2}$, both positive. Hence $x=\\log_{2}\!\left(\\frac{5\\pm\\sqrt{21}}{2}\right)$, giving two real solutions.
hints: Apply AM-GM to a^x and a^{-x}.
Equality occurs when the two terms are equal.
Substitute u=2^x to get a quadratic.
